title: Anyon Systems and Matrix Group Partner to Accelerate International Quantum Supercomputing Deployments - Quantum Computing Report
gist: Canadian full-stack superconducting vendor Anyon Systems signed KMT Technologies (Matrix Group) as exclusive distributor and authorized integration partner in strategic international markets for on-premises quantum systems bundled with HPC and AI infrastructure. Anyon is building fourth-generation control electronics with direct RDMA connectivity to GPUs and is scaling from its deployed 24-qubit MonarQ system toward a 72-qubit platform and then 100+ physical qubits.

insights.claim: Anyon is developing fourth-generation quantum control electronics that connect directly to GPU infrastructure over Remote Direct Memory Access, creating a high-bandwidth low-latency path between classical AI clusters and quantum accelerators.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Tight QPU-GPU coupling is the architectural requirement for hybrid algorithms with fast feedback loops; vendors without it are limited to batch-submitted workloads.
insights.quote: direct high-speed connectivity with GPU infrastructure using Remote Direct Memory Access (RDMA)

insights.claim: The partnership explicitly treats QPUs as specialized hardware accelerators operating inside unified HPC and AI workloads rather than as standalone quantum computers.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Framing quantum as an accelerator slot inside existing datacenter budgets is a much easier procurement sell than a standalone quantum line item — a template competitors will copy.
insights.quote: the initiative treats QPUs as specialized hardware accelerators operating inside unified HPC and AI workloads

insights.claim: The collaboration targets national governments, defense organizations, and research supercomputing centers seeking sovereign, on-premises quantum installations rather than cloud access.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Sovereign on-prem demand is a higher-ASP, lower-volume market that favors full-stack vendors and is largely insulated from cloud-quantum price competition.
insights.quote: national governments, defense organizations, and research supercomputing centers seeking sovereign, on-premises quantum installations
insights.locator: Tightly Coupled QPU-GPU Architecture via Direct RDMA

insights.claim: Anyon designs and manufactures its entire superconducting stack in-house — QPUs, cryogenic dilution refrigerators, control electronics, and the open-source Julia-based Snowflurry software suite.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Full vertical integration is exactly what sovereign buyers screen for, since it avoids foreign single-points-of-failure in the supply chain — a structural advantage in government tenders.
insights.locator: Tightly Coupled QPU-GPU Architecture via Direct RDMA

insights.claim: KMT Technologies gains exclusive distribution and authorized integration rights across strategic international markets, and will stand up regional engineering teams certified by Anyon for installation, commissioning, data center integration, and lifecycle maintenance.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Distributor-led international expansion converts fixed sales cost into channel margin, letting a small hardware vendor reach government buyers it could not serve directly.

insights.claim: Anyon's scaling path runs from its already-deployed 24-qubit MonarQ system to an upcoming 72-qubit commercial platform and then next-generation systems exceeding 100 physical qubits.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: A 24-to-72-to-100+ ladder is modest against leading superconducting roadmaps, positioning Anyon as a sovereignty and integration play rather than a raw-scale competitor.

insights.claim: The 24-qubit MonarQ is already deployed at Calcul Québec and integrated into Canada's national academic HPC network, giving Anyon operational field experience inside a live national research computing environment.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: A live national-HPC reference installation is the credential that unlocks other sovereign tenders; it is the asset the distribution deal is designed to monetize.

insights.claim: The initiative is led by Anyon Systems CEO Alireza Najafi-Yazdi and KMT Technologies CEO Moshe Azar, with KMT sitting inside the international technology integration conglomerate Matrix Group.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Backing by an established systems-integration conglomerate gives the channel real enterprise and government reach, which is usually the limiting factor for small quantum vendors.
